newsitem.title: DUBAI: UNHCR says has reports Iraq refugees enter Iran.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR says has reports Iraq refugees enter Iran.

text.p: A United Nations refugee official in Tehran said on Tuesday he had reports that Kurds fleeing factional fighting in Iraq had crossed the border into Iran.

"They are still arriving. We have reports that some have entered Iran. We don't know how many. But there still are people on the other side of the border," Laurens Jolles, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees representative in Tehran, told Reuters by telephone.
He said the refugees were fleeing towards Iran's west Azarbaijan province and Marivan border areas.
Marivan is a town in western Iran across the border from Penjwin, towards which between 70,000 and 75,000 people were fleeing on Tuesday, according to U.N. official in Turkey.
"There are large groups of people coming towards Iran. We're sending a fact-finding mission today," Jolles said.

"We've just told our people in Kermanshah and Orumiyeh that they should get going and start going towards the border," Jolles said, adding that staff were also told to leave Tehran for Sanandaj. The cities are capitals of three Iranian Kurdish-populated provinces bordering Iraq.

State-run Tehran radio on Monday quoted Ahmad Hosseini, Tehran's top official in charge of refugees, as saying Iran would make it possible for countries and international organisations to provide relief in camps in border areas. He said no refugees would be allowed into the country.
But U.N. officials said Iran has reportedly opened its borders on condition that the refugees were not armed.

Kurdistan Democratic Party guerrillas took Sulaimaniya, Iraq's biggest Kurdish city, on Monday, sealing their grip on the whole of Kurdish northern Iraq nine days after they took Arbil with the help of Iraqi troops.
